passage:
Subject: Congratulations (draft two)

Nazia,

Draft one is in my diary and starts "why her?" and that is where it is staying. This is draft two, and the part that matters is true too. When you called about the offer I screamed, and I meant it. You worked for that. It's the same company that turned me down last week, so my chest is a strange mix of warm and sour today, and I'm letting it be both.

Can you tell me how you prepared? Which case study did you use, and how did you answer the panel's question about failure? I want to learn what you did. Dinner is on me on Saturday 🎉

Shreya

qa.q: What did Shreya ask Nazia to share?
qa.a: Shreya asked how Nazia prepared, including which case study was used and how the panel's question about failure was answered.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Shreya have after the offer call?
qa.a: Shreya's chest felt warm and sour together, glad for Nazia and hurt about the company that had turned Shreya down.

qa.q: What did Shreya do with the envy, and why does that help?
qa.a: Shreya wrote the sour draft in a diary and sent an honest congratulation, so the envy did not turn into hoping Nazia would fail.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel reading this email?
qa.a: Nazia may feel warmed by the real congratulations and glad to share how the preparation went.

grounding: Shreya feels warmth and envy together when a friend gets the offer, keeps the envy private, congratulates honestly and asks how the friend prepared.

passage: The message came on the group chat while Tuan was queueing for noodles near the Sydney campus: Camila had got the graduate role at the engineering firm they had both interviewed for. Tuan typed 'congrats!!' and felt two things at once: real warmth, because Camila had helped him through second-year maths, and a sour twist in his stomach. On the walk home he caught himself thinking, 'That firm's culture is terrible anyway.' He stopped at a bench and said it out loud, quietly: 'I'm jealous.' Oddly, it helped. That evening he called Camila instead of just texting. 'I'm really happy for you. And a bit jealous, honestly.' She laughed. 'I'd be too.' 'How did you prepare for the technical round?' She talked for twenty minutes. He took notes on the back of an envelope.

qa.q: Where was Tuan when the message came?
qa.a: Tuan was queueing for noodles near the Sydney campus.

qa.q: What two feelings did Tuan have on hearing Camila's news?
qa.a: Tuan felt real warmth for Camila and a sour twist of envy at the same time.
Admitting the envy, congratulating honestly and asking how Camila prepared, because it turned envy into learning instead of sneering.

qa.q: How does Camila take Tuan's honest admission?
qa.a: Camila takes it lightly and kindly, laughing that she would feel the same, then shares twenty minutes of tips.

grounding: Shows warmth and envy together when a friend gets the offer, and the wise path of admitting it, congratulating and asking how she prepared.

passage: The placement cell at the Indore college pinned the results at noon. Pranav's name was under the bank that had rejected Sunaina in the final round. Around her, classmates slapped his back. Sunaina smiled and felt something sour rise. In the corridor she heard herself tell a friend, 'That bank has terrible hours, he'll quit in six months,' and a small, mean part of her hoped he would. Back in the empty seminar room she sat with it. Pranav had shared his notes with her all year. The sour feeling wasn't about him; it was about her own no. She wrote in her notebook: 'I'm envious. That's allowed. Being unkind isn't.' At the canteen she found Pranav. 'Congratulations, really. You earned it. Can you tell me what they asked in the last round?' He looked relieved, and pulled up a chair.

qa.q: When did the placement cell pin the results?
qa.a: The placement cell pinned the results at noon.

qa.q: What was Sunaina feeling when she saw Pranav's name?
qa.a: Sunaina felt envious and sour, even hoping for a moment that he would quit.

qa.q: What did Sunaina do that turned the envy around?
qa.a: She named it privately in her notebook, congratulated Pranav honestly, and asked what the last round covered.

qa.q: Why might Pranav look relieved when Sunaina congratulates him?
qa.a: Pranav may have worried the result would hurt their friendship, since she had been rejected by the same bank.

grounding: Shows the sour twist of envy when a batchmate gets the offer, a moment of sneering, and then private honesty and a sincere congratulation.
